From: Karen Liu <karen.liu@oasis-med.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Oasis DPA — backup/DR carve-out request (redlines attached)

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, Oasis Medical has a regulatory requirement to preserve certain system backups and snapshots for forensic and DR purposes beyond the standard customer retention window for transactional data. Weve annotated the DPA to request a carve-out that allows Oasis to require retention of encrypted backups and disaster recovery copies for up to five (5) years from creation. Our redlines are attached (Oasis_DPA_Redlines_v3.pdf).

Key asks we highlighted:
- Backup/DR copies: permitted retention up to 5 years and excluded from automated deletion triggers that apply to primary production data.
- Encryption / key handling: backups must remain encrypted; Oasis must be able to provide KMS instructions / wrap keys where feasible.
- Subprocessor access: any subprocessor storing backups must be contractually prohibited from using data except for backup/restore operations and must produce access logs on request.
- Export / transfer: we need clarity on cross-border backup copies and whether Redwood will host backups in our preferred US region.

Were prepared to proceed quickly if Redwood can: (1) accept the carve-out language with reasonable safeguards (access controls, attestation/reporting), and (2) commit to execution via DocuSign once final wording is agreed.

Im looping in Tom Rivera (Oasis procurement) and our outside counsel at Bates for any contract/legal clarifications. Can you confirm whether your legal/privacy team can accept our suggested retention cap and whether youd require different controls for Dedicated or Private deployment models?

Thanks,

Karen Liu
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Oasis Medical

Folks — forwarding Oasis request. Theyre asking for a 5-year retention cap for backups/DR copies that would be excluded from automatic deletion of primary data. They also want (i) KMS/key wrap options, (ii) subprocessor access limitation and logging, and (iii) region guarantee for backup storage.

My thoughts / potential options:
1) Accept limited carve-out with controls (recommended):
   - Add clause: "Backup and disaster recovery copies created in the ordinary course of Redwoods operations and retained solely for the purpose of disaster recovery and forensic investigation (\"DR Copies\") may be retained for a period not to exceed five (5) years from creation. Redwood will maintain technical and organizational measures proportional to the sensitivity of Customer Data, including encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access controls, and access logging for DR Copies."
   - Require Oasis to provide written KMS requirements; offer two options: Redwood-managed KMS with customer-specific key isolation, or customer-managed keys in Dedicated/Private deployments.
   - Subprocessor language: ensure subprocessors are prohibited from using Customer Data other than to provide backup/DR services; Redwood will provide attestation and access logs on a quarterly or ad-hoc basis for justified requests.
   - Region guarantee: for Hosted customers, well commit to storing backups in the customers primary jurisdiction (US region) unless otherwise agreed.

2) Narrow carve-out (conservative): allow retention only to the extent required for DR (shorter period, e.g., 18 months) and require more aggressive access controls / SOC2 evidence.

Risks / asks for Legal: please review the draft language above and confirm:
- Is the 5-year cap acceptable from a Redwood legal risk perspective?
- Any suggested limits on when Oasis can request access logs or require attestations?
- Does this create an open-ended obligation to store backups in perpetuity via follow-on requests?

Attachments: Redline_Summary.xlsx (Ive summarized the redlines and impact matrix). I can join a quick call with Karen/Tom if helpful.

Thanks — Alex

We reviewed Redwoods proposed carve-out language. Our client appreciates the proposed safeguards. A few comments from counsel:

- Subprocessors: Bates requests explicit language that any subprocessor storing DR copies will be contractually restricted to backup and restore activities only, and Redwood must provide customer-specific written confirmations that those subprocessors have no rights to use Customer Data for secondary processing.
- Access logs / audit: Oasis requests a clause allowing for quarterly attestation of subprocessor access logs or access to such logs within 10 business days upon reasonable request, subject to confidentiality constraints.
- Key management: we prefer an option that allows Oasis to insist on customer-managed keys (BYOK) when backups are destined for long-term retention beyond 12 months. If BYOK is unavailable on Hosted, we would like a security attestation and a signed representation of key isolation.

We have revised the language slightly in the attached redline and propose to proceed to DocuSign if Redwood can accept these edits with minor tweaks. Please confirm the point of contact at Redwood to finalize the DocuSign envelope.

Karen / Tom —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and Bates notes. Weve reviewed internally with Legal and Privacy and can accept the carve-out with the following binding commitments:

- Retention cap: Redwood will permit DR Copies to be retained up to five (5) years from creation when Oasis identifies such backups as subject to the carve-out.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will require subprocessors that store DR Copies to be contractually limited to backup and restore activities and will provide attestation of such contractual terms.
- Audit & logs: Redwood will provide access log extracts for DR Copy access upon reasonable request; for routine assurance, Redwood will provide quarterly attestations. For ad-hoc forensic requests, Redwood will respond within 10 business days where possible.
- KMS: For Hosted customers, Redwood offers a managed-key option with documented key isolation; for Dedicated/Private, BYOK (customer-managed keys) is available and will be the default where requested for long-term backup retention.
- Region: Redwood will store DR Copies in the customers primary US region by default; cross-border storage requires explicit written agreement.

If that aligns with Oasis expectations, well (1) incorporate the final redline, (2) prepare the DocuSign envelope, and (3) route to your signatories and our authorized signatory from Legal.
